From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pipeline health: gap pressure & commit cadence — Q3 forecast prep

Team,

Quick note ahead of next week's forecast lock: finance flagged a 12% shortfall in our Q3 commit compared to the last run. I pulled a snapshot (attached) and highlighted a set of ~14 opportunities that are currently overstated by stage/probability or missing recent activity. We need a fast hygiene pass so the forecast reflects reality.

Ask (short and specific):
- Owners (Karthik/Naomi/Laura): update stage & next-step in SFDC for deals listed on tab "ActionFlags" by WED 6/19 EOD PT. If a deal is no longer live, move to Lost and set loss reason.
- For any deal you still intend to include, set a commit date and confirm the expected close week in the comment column.
- I will run a reconciled rollup on THU morning and share back the adjusted roll-forward with Finance.

Attachments: pipeline_snapshot_Q3.xlsx (master snapshot), commit_rollup_slide.pdf (slot for Thurs). I've also exported the quick flags csv for easy ingest (emailed_pipeline_flags.csv).

Priority areas:
- Large mid-market deals (> $250k ARR) where stage hasn’t changed in >30 days
- Recent technical/legal blockers logged without an update
- Deals with improbable close dates (e.g., dated beyond Q3 but marked commit)

Keep the replies short — just confirm you got this and call out any blockers that prevent you from making the updates by WED.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pipeline_snapshot_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1.2 MB)]
[Attachment: commit_rollup_slide.pdf (presentation, 420 KB)]

- Update stages and add commit weeks for the 6 largest deals by EOD today.

Still unclear on one item: for deals with POC completed and a buyer-run procurement that has no PO date, should we default to mid-Q3 or hold to "At Risk" until a procurement timeline is confirmed? Finance input appreciated.

Karthik

Thanks Marcus — I reviewed the ActionFlags tab and pulled notes for our top 8 deals. Quick summary:

- ACME Analytics (ACME-2029-Q3-01): POC complete, legal has an outstanding SOW question. Sales owner estimates 75% but procurement has not confirmed PO week. I recommend we leave at 60% commit and note the procurement risk.
- Stonebridge (STB-334): Sales still optimistic but sales activity shows no exec sponsor engagement in 45 days. Recommend moving to "Commit — At Risk" and reduce to 40%.
- NorthBridge (NB-77): Two-week procurement window confirmed; push close to week of 8/5 and mark commit accordingly.

I attached a CSV with my flags and brief notes (emailed_pipeline_flags.csv).

On the procurement question Karthik asked: Finance prefers conservative assumptions for forecast lock. If procurement has not provided a firm PO week, default to "At Risk" and use a lower probability (40–60%) unless the buyer provides a confirmed PO date. Jill/David — please confirm if Finance can accept this rule for the lock.

I can jump on a 15-min call tomorrow morning if we need to adjudicate specific deals before WED.

Naomi
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up. From ACME's side: procurement is still collecting final signature approvals across two business units. We expect a PO by the end of July, but I can't guarantee a week. The sales sponsor is pushing a mid-July target.

Given that, I agree with Naomi's practical approach — mark ACME as "At Risk" for the Q3 lock with a note that procurement is likely to deliver in late July, which would push billing into Q3/Q4 boundary. If Redwood needs a deterministic number for planning, I'd be happy to join the Thursday call and provide a live status update.
